Using it with a currency that has no rate is an error, and using it with the base currency shows the usual amounts.

Everything else should keep working as it does now.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

"""Command-line interface: argument parsing, JSON output, errors as exit status 1."""

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import sys
from typing import List, Optional

from kitty import ledger, storage
from kitty.errors import KittyError
from kitty.money import fmt


class _Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message):
        raise KittyError(f"{message}\n{self.format_usage().rstrip()}")


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = _Parser(prog="python3 -m kitty", description="Track shared expenses on group trips.")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND", parser_class=_Parser)
    sub.required = True

    init = sub.add_parser("init", help="start a new kitty")
    init.add_argument("currency")

    member = sub.add_parser("member", help="manage members")
    msub = member.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    msub.required = True
    msub.add_parser("add").add_argument("name")
    msub.add_parser("remove").add_argument("name")
    msub.add_parser("list")

    expense = sub.add_parser("expense", help="manage expenses")
    esub = expense.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    esub.required = True
    add = esub.add_parser("add")
    add.add_argument("payer")
    add.add_argument("amount")
    add.add_argument("description")
    for opt in ["among", "exact", "shares", "percent", "currency", "date", "category"]:
        add.add_argument(f"--{opt}")
    esub.add_parser("list")
    esub.add_parser("remove").add_argument("id")

    payment = sub.add_parser("payment", help="record a repayment")
    psub = payment.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    psub.required = True
    padd = psub.add_parser("add")
    padd.add_argument("frm", metavar="from")
    padd.add_argument("to")
    padd.add_argument("amount")
    padd.add_argument("--currency")
    padd.add_argument("--date")

    rate = sub.add_parser("rate", help="set exchange rates")
    rsub = rate.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    rsub.required = True
    rset = rsub.add_parser("set")
    rset.add_argument("currency")
    rset.add_argument("rate")

    sub.add_parser("balances", help="show each person's balance")
    sub.add_parser("settle", help="suggest payments to square up")
    sub.add_parser("history", help="entries affecting one person").add_argument("name")
    sub.add_parser("report", help="spending per category")
    sub.add_parser("export", help="write expenses to CSV").add_argument("file")
    return p


def _expense_view(e: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        "id": e["id"], "date": e["date"], "payer": e["payer"], "description": e["description"],
        "amount": fmt(e["amount"]), "currency": e["currency"], "base_amount": fmt(e["base_amount"]),
        "category": e["category"], "shares": {n: fmt(c) for n, c in e["shares"]},
    }


def _export(state: dict, path: str) -> None:
    if os.path.realpath(path) == os.path.realpath(storage.FILENAME):
        raise KittyError(f"refusing to overwrite {storage.FILENAME} with the export")
    try:
        with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            w = csv.writer(f)
            w.writerow(["id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency",
                        "category", "base_amount"])
            for e in state["expenses"]:
                w.writerow([e["id"], e["date"], e["payer"], e["description"], fmt(e["amount"]),
                            e["currency"], e["category"], fmt(e["base_amount"])])
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot write {path}: {e.strerror or e}") from None


def _run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    """Run one command. Returns output to print as JSON, a raw string, or None."""
    if args.command == "init":
        if storage.exists():
            raise KittyError(f"{storage.FILENAME} already exists here")
        storage.save(ledger.new_state(args.currency))
        return None

    state = storage.load()
    cmd = (args.command, getattr(args, "action", None))
    result = None  # type: object
    changed = True

    if cmd == ("member", "add"):
        ledger.add_member(state, args.name)
    elif cmd == ("member", "remove"):
        ledger.remove_member(state, args.name)
    elif cmd == ("expense", "add"):
        result = str(ledger.add_expense(
            state, args.payer, args.amount, args.description, among=args.among, exact=args.exact,
            shares=args.shares, percent=args.percent, currency=args.currency, date=args.date,
            category=args.category))
    elif cmd == ("expense", "remove"):
        ledger.remove_expense(state, args.id)
    elif cmd == ("payment", "add"):
        ledger.add_payment(state, args.frm, args.to, args.amount,
                           currency=args.currency, date=args.date)
    elif cmd == ("rate", "set"):
        ledger.set_rate(state, args.currency, args.rate)
    else:
        changed = False
        if cmd == ("member", "list"):
            result = list(state["members"])
        elif cmd == ("expense", "list"):
            result = [_expense_view(e) for e in state["expenses"]]
        elif args.command == "balances":
            result = {n: fmt(c) for n, c in ledger.balances(state).items()}
        elif args.command == "settle":
            result = [{"from": f, "to": t, "amount": fmt(c)} for f, t, c in ledger.settle(state)]
        elif args.command == "history":
            result = [dict(h, change=fmt(h["change"]), balance=fmt(h["balance"]))
                      for h in ledger.history(state, args.name)]
        elif args.command == "report":
            result = {cat: {n: fmt(c) for n, c in people.items()}
                      for cat, people in ledger.report(state).items()}
        elif args.command == "export":
            _export(state, args.file)

    if changed:
        storage.save(state)
    return result


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    try:
        args = _build_parser().parse_args(argv)
        result = _run(args)
    except KittyError as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if isinstance(result, str):
        print(result)
    elif result is not None:
        print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 0

18	    if not _AMOUNT.fullmatch(text):
19	        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (use a positive number with at most two decimals)")
20	    whole, _, frac = text.partition(".")
21	    cents = int(whole) * 100 + int(frac.ljust(2, "0"))

23	        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (must be greater than zero)")

39	    return int(text)

51	    return text.upper()

56	        if not _DATE.fullmatch(text):
57	            raise ValueError

63	
64	def convert(cents: int, rate: Decimal) -> int:
65	    """Convert to base cents: amount x rate, rounded to the cent, halves up.
66	
67	    Exact integer arithmetic, so no Decimal precision limit applies.
68	    """
69	    num, den = rate.as_integer_ratio()
70	    return (2 * cents * num + den) // (2 * den)
71	
72	
73	def split_weighted(total: int, weights: List[Tuple[str, int]]) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
74	    """Round each exact portion down, then hand out leftover cents in list order."""
75	    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
76	    parts = [[name, total * w // weight_sum] for name, w in weights]
77	    leftover = total - sum(c for _, c in parts)
78	    for i in range(leftover):
79	        parts[i][1] += 1
80	    return [(name, cents) for name, cents in parts]
81	
82	
83	def split_equal(total: int, names: List[str]) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
84	    return split_weighted(total, [(name, 1) for name in names])
85	
86	
87	def fmt(cents: int) -> str:
88	    sign = "-" if cents < 0 else ""
89	    whole, frac = divmod(abs(cents), 100)
90	    return f"{sign}{whole}.{frac:02d}"
91

1	"""Reading and atomically writing kitty.json."""
2	
3	import json
4	import os
5	import tempfile
6	
7	from kitty import money
8	from kitty.errors import KittyError
9	
10	FILENAME = "kitty.json"
11	
12	
13	def _path(directory: str) -> str:
14	    return os.path.join(directory, FILENAME)
15	
16	
17	def exists(directory: str = ".") -> bool:
18	    return os.path.exists(_path(directory))
19	
20	
21	def load(directory: str = ".") -> dict:
22	    path = _path(directory)
23	    if not os.path.exists(path):
24	        raise KittyError(f"no {FILENAME} here; run init first")
25	    try:
26	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
27	            state = json.load(f)
28	    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, RecursionError) as e:
29	        raise KittyError(f"cannot read {FILENAME}: {e}") from None
30	    if not _well_formed(state):
31	        raise KittyError(f"cannot read {FILENAME}: it is damaged or not a kitty file")
32	    return state
33	
34	
35	def _is_int(v) -> bool:
36	    return isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool)
37	
38	
39	def _has(entry, fields: dict) -> bool:
40	    return isinstance(entry, dict) and all(
41	        k in entry and (_is_int(entry[k]) if t is int else isinstance(entry[k], t))
42	        for k, t in fields.items())
43	
44	
45	_TOP = {"base": str, "rates": dict, "members": list, "next_id": int, "next_seq": int,
46	        "expenses": list, "payments": list}
47	_ENTRY = {"seq": int, "date": str, "amount": int, "currency": str, "rate": str,
48	          "base_amount": int}
49	_EXPENSE = dict(_ENTRY, id=int, payer=str, description=str, category=str, shares=list)
50	_PAYMENT = dict(_ENTRY, **{"from": str, "to": str})
51	
52	
53	def _well_formed(state) -> bool:
54	    if not _has(state, _TOP):
55	        return False
56	    members = state["members"]
57	    if not all(isinstance(m, str) for m in members):
58	        return False
59	    try:
60	        money.parse_currency(state["base"])
61	        for code, rate in state["rates"].items():
62	            money.parse_currency(code)
63	            money.parse_rate(rate)
64	    except (KittyError, TypeError):
65	        return False
66	    for e in state["expenses"]:
67	        if not _has(e, _EXPENSE) or e["payer"] not in members:
68	            return False
69	        for share in e["shares"]:
70	            if not (isinstance(share, list) and len(share) == 2 and share[0] in members
71	                    and _is_int(share[1])):
72	                return False
73	    return all(_has(p, _PAYMENT) and p["from"] in members and p["to"] in members
74	               for p in state["payments"])
75	
76	
77	def save(state: dict, directory: str = ".") -> None:
78	    tmp_name = None
79	    try:
80	        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", encoding="utf-8", dir=directory, prefix=".kitty-",
81	                                         suffix=".tmp", delete=False) as tmp:
82	            tmp_name = tmp.name
83	            json.dump(state, tmp, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
84	            tmp.write("\n")
85	        os.chmod(tmp_name, 0o644)
86	        os.replace(tmp_name, _path(directory))
87	    except OSError as e:
88	        if tmp_name and os.path.exists(tmp_name):
89	            os.unlink(tmp_name)
90	        raise KittyError(f"cannot write {FILENAME}: {e.strerror or e}") from None
91

83	    try:

95	def _run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
96	    """Run one command. Returns output to print as JSON, a raw string, or None."""
97	    if args.command == "init":
98	        if storage.exists():
99	            raise KittyError(f"{storage.FILENAME} already exists here")
100	        storage.save(ledger.new_state(args.currency))
101	        return None
102	
103	    state = storage.load()
104	    cmd = (args.command, getattr(args, "action", None))
105	    result = None  # type: object
106	    changed = True
107	
108	    if cmd == ("member", "add"):
109	        ledger.add_member(state, args.name)
110	    elif cmd == ("member", "remove"):
111	        ledger.remove_member(state, args.name)
112	    elif cmd == ("expense", "add"):
113	        result = str(ledger.add_expense(
114	            state, args.payer, args.amount, args.description, among=args.among, exact=args.exact,
115	            shares=args.shares, percent=args.percent, currency=args.currency, date=args.date,
116	            category=args.category))
117	    elif cmd == ("expense", "remove"):
118	        ledger.remove_expense(state, args.id)
119	    elif cmd == ("payment", "add"):
120	        ledger.add_payment(state, args.frm, args.to, args.amount,
121	                           currency=args.currency, date=args.date)
122	    elif cmd == ("rate", "set"):
123	        ledger.set_rate(state, args.currency, args.rate)
124	    else:
125	        changed = False
126	        if cmd == ("member", "list"):
127	            result = list(state["members"])
128	        elif cmd == ("expense", "list"):
129	            result = [_expense_view(e) for e in state["expenses"]]
130	        elif args.command == "balances":
131	            result = {n: fmt(c) for n, c in ledger.balances(state).items()}
132	        elif args.command == "settle":
133	            result = [{"from": f, "to": t, "amount": fmt(c)} for f, t, c in ledger.settle(state)]
134	        elif args.command == "history":
135	            result = [dict(h, change=fmt(h["change"]), balance=fmt(h["balance"]))
136	                      for h in ledger.history(state, args.name)]
137	        elif args.command == "report":
138	            result = {cat: {n: fmt(c) for n, c in people.items()}
139	                      for cat, people in ledger.report(state).items()}
140	        elif args.command == "export":
141	            _export(state, args.file)
142	
143	    if changed:
144	        storage.save(state)
145	    return result
146	
147	
148	def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
149	    try:
150	        args = _build_parser().parse_args(argv)
151	        result = _run(args)
152	    except KittyError as e:
153	        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
154	        return 1
155	    if isinstance(result, str):
156	        print(result)
157	    elif result is not None:
158	        print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))
159	    return 0

1	"""Ledger operations on the plain-dict state. All money values are integer cents."""
2	
3	import datetime
4	from decimal import Decimal
5	from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
6	
7	from kitty import money
8	from kitty.errors import KittyError
9	
10	
11	def new_state(base_text: str) -> dict:
12	    return {
13	        "base": money.parse_currency(base_text),
14	        "rates": {},
15	        "members": [],
16	        "next_id": 1,
17	        "next_seq": 1,
18	        "expenses": [],
19	        "payments": [],
20	    }
21	
22	
23	def resolve(state: dict, name: str) -> str:
24	    key = name.strip().casefold()
25	    for member in state["members"]:
26	        if member.casefold() == key:
27	            return member
28	    raise KittyError(f"unknown member: {name}")
29	
30	
31	def add_member(state: dict, name: str) -> None:
32	    name = name.strip()
33	    if not name:
34	        raise KittyError("member name cannot be empty")
35	    if "," in name or "=" in name:
36	        raise KittyError(f"member name cannot contain ',' or '=': {name}")
37	    if any(m.casefold() == name.casefold() for m in state["members"]):
38	        raise KittyError(f"member already exists: {name}")
39	    state["members"].append(name)
40	
41	
42	def _is_referenced(state: dict, name: str) -> bool:
43	    for e in state["expenses"]:
44	        if e["payer"] == name or any(n == name for n, _ in e["shares"]):
45	            return True
46	    return any(p["from"] == name or p["to"] == name for p in state["payments"])
47	
48	
49	def remove_member(state: dict, name: str) -> None:
50	    member = resolve(state, name)
51	    if _is_referenced(state, member):
52	        raise KittyError(f"cannot remove {member}: they appear in expenses or payments")
53	    state["members"].remove(member)
54	
55	
56	def set_rate(state: dict, code_text: str, rate_text: str) -> None:
57	    code = money.parse_currency(code_text)
58	    if code == state["base"]:
59	        raise KittyError(f"{code} is the base currency; its rate is always 1")
60	    state["rates"][code] = str(money.parse_rate(rate_text))
61	
62	
63	def rate_for(state: dict, code: str) -> Decimal:
64	    if code == state["base"]:
65	        return Decimal(1)
66	    if code not in state["rates"]:
67	        raise KittyError(f"no rate set for {code}; use: rate set {code} RATE")
68	    return Decimal(state["rates"][code])
69	
70	
71	def _resolve_unique(state: dict, names: List[str]) -> List[str]:
72	    resolved = [resolve(state, n) for n in names]
73	    for i, name in enumerate(resolved):
74	        if name in resolved[:i]:
75	            raise KittyError(f"{name} is listed more than once")
76	    return resolved
77	
78	
79	def _parse_pairs(state: dict, text: str,
80	                 parse_value: Callable[[str], int]) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
81	    names, values = [], []
82	    for item in text.split(","):
83	        if "=" not in item:
84	            raise KittyError(f"expected NAME=VALUE, got: {item!r}")
85	        name, value = item.split("=", 1)
86	        names.append(name)
87	        values.append(parse_value(value.strip()))
88	    return list(zip(_resolve_unique(state, names), values))
89	
90	
91	def _convert_amount(state: dict, amount_text: str,
92	                    currency: Optional[str]) -> Tuple[int, str, Decimal, int]:
93	    amount = money.parse_amount(amount_text)
94	    code = state["base"] if currency is None else money.parse_currency(currency)
95	    rate = rate_for(state, code)
96	    base_amount = money.convert(amount, rate)
97	    if base_amount == 0:
98	        raise KittyError(f"{money.fmt(amount)} {code} is less than one cent in {state['base']}")
99	    return amount, code, rate, base_amount
100	
101	
102	def _next_seq(state: dict) -> int:
103	    seq = state["next_seq"]
104	    state["next_seq"] += 1
105	    return seq
106	
107	
108	def add_expense(state: dict, payer: str, amount_text: str, description: str, *,
109	                among: Optional[str] = None, exact: Optional[str] = None,
110	                shares: Optional[str] = None, percent: Optional[str] = None,
111	                currency: Optional[str] = None, date: Optional[str] = None,
112	                category: Optional[str] = None) -> int:
113	    chosen = [opt for opt, v in [("--among", among), ("--exact", exact),
114	                                 ("--shares", shares), ("--percent", percent)] if v is not None]
115	    if len(chosen) > 1:
116	        raise KittyError(f"use only one of {', '.join(chosen)}")
117	    payer = resolve(state, payer)
118	    amount, code, rate, total = _convert_amount(state, amount_text, currency)
119	    day = datetime.date.today().isoformat() if date is None else money.parse_date(date)
120	
121	    if exact is not None:
122	        pairs = _parse_pairs(state, exact, money.parse_amount)
123	        if sum(v for _, v in pairs) != amount:
124	            raise KittyError(f"--exact amounts add up to {money.fmt(sum(v for _, v in pairs))}, "
125	                             f"not {money.fmt(amount)}")
126	        split = money.split_weighted(total, pairs)
127	    elif percent is not None:
128	        pairs = _parse_pairs(state, percent, money.parse_percent)
129	        if sum(v for _, v in pairs) != 10000:
130	            raise KittyError(f"--percent values add up to {money.fmt(sum(v for _, v in pairs))}, not 100")
131	        split = money.split_weighted(total, pairs)
132	    elif shares is not None:
133	        split = money.split_weighted(total, _parse_pairs(state, shares, money.parse_share))
134	    else:
135	        names = state["members"] if among is None else _resolve_unique(state, among.split(","))
136	        if not names:
137	            raise KittyError("there are no members to split the expense among")
138	        split = money.split_equal(total, names)
139	
140	    expense_id = state["next_id"]
141	    state["next_id"] += 1
142	    state["expenses"].append({
143	        "id": expense_id, "seq": _next_seq(state), "date": day, "payer": payer,
144	        "description": description, "amount": amount, "currency": code, "rate": str(rate),
145	        "base_amount": total, "category": "other" if category is None else category,
146	        "shares": [[name, cents] for name, cents in split],
147	    })
148	    return expense_id
149	
150	
151	def remove_expense(state: dict, id_text: str) -> None:
152	    for i, e in enumerate(state["expenses"]):
153	        if str(e["id"]) == id_text.strip():
154	            del state["expenses"][i]
155	            return
156	    raise KittyError(f"no expense with ID {id_text}")
157	
158	
159	def add_payment(state: dict, frm: str, to: str, amount_text: str, *,
160	                currency: Optional[str] = None, date: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
161	    frm, to = resolve(state, frm), resolve(state, to)
162	    if frm == to:
163	        raise KittyError(f"{frm} cannot pay themselves")
164	    amount, code, rate, base_amount = _convert_amount(state, amount_text, currency)
165	    day = datetime.date.today().isoformat() if date is None else money.parse_date(date)
166	    state["payments"].append({
167	        "seq": _next_seq(state), "date": day, "from": frm, "to": to, "amount": amount,
168	        "currency": code, "rate": str(rate), "base_amount": base_amount,
169	    })
170	
171	
172	def _changes(state: dict, name: str) -> List[Tuple[str, int, str, int]]:
173	    """(date, seq, description, change) for each entry that touches `name`."""
174	    out = []
175	    for e in state["expenses"]:
176	        share = sum(c for n, c in e["shares"] if n == name)
177	        paid = e["base_amount"] if e["payer"] == name else 0
178	        if e["payer"] == name or any(n == name for n, _ in e["shares"]):
179	            out.append((e["date"], e["seq"], e["description"], paid - share))
180	    for p in state["payments"]:
181	        if p["from"] == name:
182	            out.append((p["date"], p["seq"], f"Payment to {p['to']}", p["base_amount"]))
183	        elif p["to"] == name:
184	            out.append((p["date"], p["seq"], f"Payment from {p['from']}", -p["base_amount"]))
185	    return out
186	
187	
188	def balances(state: dict) -> Dict[str, int]:
189	    bal = {name: 0 for name in state["members"]}
190	    for e in state["expenses"]:
191	        bal[e["payer"]] += e["base_amount"]
192	        for name, cents in e["shares"]:
193	            bal[name] -= cents
194	    for p in state["payments"]:
195	        bal[p["from"]] += p["base_amount"]
196	        bal[p["to"]] -= p["base_amount"]
197	    return bal
198	
199	
200	def settle(state: dict) -> List[Tuple[str, str, int]]:
201	    bal = {n: c for n, c in balances(state).items() if c != 0}
202	    out = []
203	    while bal:
204	        debtor = min((n for n in bal if bal[n] < 0), key=lambda n: (bal[n], n.casefold()))
205	        creditor = min((n for n in bal if bal[n] > 0), key=lambda n: (-bal[n], n.casefold()))
206	        amount = min(-bal[debtor], bal[creditor])
207	        out.append((debtor, creditor, amount))
208	        bal[debtor] += amount
209	        bal[creditor] -= amount
210	        bal = {n: c for n, c in bal.items() if c != 0}
211	    return out
212	
213	
214	def history(state: dict, name: str) -> List[dict]:
215	    member = resolve(state, name)
216	    running = 0
217	    out = []
218	    for day, _, description, change in sorted(_changes(state, member), key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1])):
219	        running += change
220	        out.append({"date": day, "description": description, "change": change, "balance": running})
221	    return out
222	
223	
224	def report(state: dict) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, int]]:
225	    totals = {}  # type: Dict[str, Dict[str, int]]
226	    for e in state["expenses"]:
227	        cat = totals.setdefault(e["category"], {})
228	        for name, cents in e["shares"]:
229	            cat[name] = cat.get(name, 0) + cents
230	    order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(state["members"])}
231	    return {c: {n: totals[c][n] for n in sorted(totals[c], key=order.__getitem__)}
232	            for c in sorted(totals)}

1	"""Money rules: parsing, conversion and splitting, all on integer cents."""
2	
3	import datetime
4	import re
5	from decimal import Decimal
6	from typing import List, Tuple
7	
8	from kitty.errors import KittyError
9	
10	_AMOUNT = re.compile(r"\d+(\.\d{1,2})?")
11	_RATE = re.compile(r"\d+(\.\d+)?")
12	_INT = re.compile(r"\d+")
13	_CURRENCY = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]{3}")
14	_DATE = re.compile(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}")
15	
16	
17	def _cents(text: str, what: str) -> int:
18	    if not _AMOUNT.fullmatch(text):
19	        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (use a positive number with at most two decimals)")
20	    whole, _, frac = text.partition(".")
21	    cents = int(whole) * 100 + int(frac.ljust(2, "0"))
22	    if cents <= 0:
23	        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (must be greater than zero)")
24	    return cents
25	
26	
27	def parse_amount(text: str) -> int:
28	    return _cents(text, "amount")
29

# kitty — shared trip expenses: design

## Intent

Friends on group trips currently settle up with spreadsheets and arguments at
the end. `kitty` replaces that with something **simple and predictable**: a
command-line tool that records who paid what, how each cost is split, and at
the end says who owes whom. Every number it prints must be reproducible by
hand from the rules below — no hidden rounding, no surprising re-computation.

## Goals

- Record members, expenses (with flexible splits and currencies) and repayments.
- Show balances, a deterministic settle-up plan, per-person history, a
  per-category spending report, and a CSV export.
- Scriptable: reporting commands print JSON in fixed shapes.
- Robust: bad input is a clean error, never a traceback, never a corrupted file.

## Non-goals

- Fewest-possible-payments optimisation (settle uses a specific greedy method).
- Live exchange rates, multiple kitties per folder, editing entries in place
  (remove and re-add instead), listing/removing payments (not requested; can
  be added later), any third-party dependency.

## Anti-goals (would be a failure even if it "works")

- Balances that don't sum to exactly zero, or that change on their own
  (e.g. because a rate was changed later).
- Floating-point arithmetic anywhere in money handling.
- An error that leaves `kitty.json` partially written or modified.

## Constraints

- Python standard library only. Must run on **Python 3.9** (the installed
  version is 3.9.6) — no `match`, no `X | Y` type syntax at runtime.
- Run as `python3 -m kitty <command>` from the project folder (package `kitty/`
  with `__main__.py`).
- All state in `kitty.json` in the current working directory.

## Approaches considered

1. **Small package with separated layers (chosen).** `money.py` (parsing,
   conversion, cent-splitting — pure functions on int cents / `Decimal`),
   `ledger.py` (members, expenses, payments, balances, settle, history,
   report — pure logic over loaded data), `storage.py` (read/write
   `kitty.json`), `cli.py` (argparse, JSON output, error → exit 1). Tests with
   `unittest`, both unit-level on the money rules and end-to-end through the
   real command in a temp directory. Chosen because the rounding rules are what
   the user most needs to trust, so they must be isolated and directly tested.
2. **Event log, recompute everything on each run.** Little benefit because
   rates and splits are locked at record time; adds a way for results to drift.
3. **Single-file script.** Faster to write, but mixes money logic with CLI
   parsing and fights the `python3 -m kitty` package layout.

## Data rules (decided by the user)

### Money and amounts
- All arithmetic uses `Decimal` / integer cents. Never floats.
- An amount argument must be a positive number with at most two decimal
  places. `12.345`, `0`, `-5`, `abc` are errors (no rounding of input).
- Output money is a string with exactly two decimals, e.g. `"41.40"`,
  `"-20.70"`.

### Currencies and rates
- Currency codes are three letters, accepted in any case, stored uppercase.
- `init EUR` sets the base currency. The base currency always has rate 1.
- `rate set USD 0.92` means 1 USD = 0.92 base. Setting a rate for the base
  currency is an error. Rate must be a positive decimal.
- Conversion: `amount × rate`, rounded to the cent, **halves rounded up**
  (`ROUND_HALF_UP`).
- Each expense and payment **stores the rate in force when it was added** and
  its converted base amount. Later `rate set` never changes existing entries.
- Using a currency with no rate set is an error.

### Splitting (always in base-currency cents, after conversion)
Let `T` be the converted base total in cents.
- **Equal (default: everyone)**: participants are all current members in the
  order they joined. Each gets `floor(T / n)`; the leftover cents go one each
  to participants in order. 10.00 among Alice, Bob, Cara → 3.34, 3.33, 3.33.
- **`--among A,B`**: same as equal, among only those listed, in the order
  listed.
- **`--shares A=2,B=1`**: weights are positive whole numbers. Each portion is
  `floor(T × w / Σw)`; leftover cents go one each in listed order.
  10.00 with `A=1,B=2` → A 3.34, B 6.66.
- **`--percent A=60,B=40`**: values must total exactly 100; handled as
  weights exactly like shares (portion `floor(T × p / 100)`, leftovers in
  listed order).
- **`--exact A=30,B=20`**: values are in the expense's own currency and must
  add up exactly to the expense amount (else error); then they are treated as
  weights on `T` exactly like shares.
- Only one of `--among`, `--exact`, `--shares`, `--percent` per expense.
- Every name in a split must be a current member; no name may appear twice.
- Splits are computed **once, when the expense is added**, and stored. Members
  who join later are not part of earlier "everyone" expenses.
- Shares therefore always sum to exactly `T`.

### Members
- Names are **case-insensitive**: "alice" and "Alice" are the same person.
  Adding a name that matches an existing one case-insensitively is an error.
  Every command accepts any spelling; output always uses the name as first
  added.
- Names may not contain `,` or `=`. (Builder's call: also reject empty /
  whitespace-only names.)
- Join order is preserved and matters (equal splits, output order).
- `member remove` is refused if the person appears anywhere: as payer or
  sharer of any expense, or sender/recipient of any payment. Removing someone
  with no history is fine.

### Payments
- `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT [--currency C] [--date D]`: FROM's balance goes
  up by the base amount, TO's goes down. FROM and TO the same person is an
  error. Both must be members.

### Balances
- For each member: `Σ(base amounts they paid) − Σ(their shares) +
  Σ(payments sent) − Σ(payments received)`. Positive = owed money.

### Settle (greedy, deterministic)
While anyone has a nonzero balance: the person who owes the most (most
negative) pays the person who is owed the most (most positive) the smaller of
the two absolute amounts, so at least one of them reaches zero. Ties on either
side go to the name that comes first alphabetically, ignoring case
(`str.casefold`). Payments are listed in the order they are worked out.
`settle` only suggests; it records nothing.

### Dates and categories
- `--date YYYY-MM-DD`, validated as a real date; default is today.
- `--category`, default `"other"`.

### IDs
- Expenses are numbered 1, 2, 3, … ; an ID is never reused, even after
  removal (store a `next_id` counter).

## Commands and output

Reporting commands print JSON via `json.dumps` with default separators (which
matches the examples below exactly), followed by a newline.

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `init CUR` | nothing |
| `member add NAME` / `member remove NAME` | nothing |
| `member list` | `["Alice", "Bob"]` (join order) |
| `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION [opts]` | the new ID alone, e.g. `1` |
| `expense list` | see below (ID order) |
| `expense remove ID` | nothing; unknown ID is an error |
| `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT [--currency] [--date]` | nothing |
| `rate set CUR RATE` | nothing |
| `balances` | `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}` |
| `settle` | `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]` |
| `history NAME` | `[{"date": ..., "description": ..., "change": ..., "balance": ...}]` |
| `report` | `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}` |
| `export FILE` | nothing; writes CSV |

`expense list` entry:
`{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner",
"amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category":
"food", "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}` — `amount` is in the
expense's own currency, everything else in base. `shares` keys are in split
order.

`history NAME`: every expense where the person is payer or sharer, and every
payment they sent or received, sorted by date then by the order added
(expenses and payments share one insertion sequence). `change` is their
balance change from that entry; `balance` is the running total. Expense lines
use the expense description; payments use `"Payment to Alice"` (sender's view)
or `"Payment from Bob"` (recipient's view). A payer with no share still gets a
line. The final `balance` equals that person's `balances` value.

`report`: for each category, each person's total **share** (not what they
paid) of expenses in that category. Payments are excluded.

`export FILE`: CSV with header `id,date,payer,description,amount,currency,category,base_amount`,
one row per expense in ID order, money as two-decimal strings. Overwrites
FILE if it exists.

## Errors

- Any error: message to **stderr**, exit status **1**, and `kitty.json` is
  **left unchanged** (validate fully before writing; write atomically via a
  temp file + rename).
- Includes argparse usage errors (override its default exit status 2).
- Any command other than `init` when `kitty.json` doesn't exist is an error;
  `init` when it already exists is an error.
- An unreadable or malformed `kitty.json` is an error, not a traceback.

## Storage

`kitty.json` (builder may refine the exact schema): base currency, rates
(as decimal strings), members in join order, expenses and payments each with a
shared insertion sequence number, stored rate, original amount in cents,
base amount in cents, and stored shares as an ordered list of `[name, cents]`;
plus `next_id`. Money stored as integer cents so nothing is re-rounded on
reload.

## Calls I made (user can override)

- Mutating commands other than `expense add` print nothing on success.
- `report`: categories in alphabetical order; within each, only people who
  had a share in that category, in join order. `balances` includes every
  current member, in join order.
- Category is stored as typed (so `Food` and `food` are different categories).
- Rates may have any number of decimal places.
- `--percent` values may have up to two decimals (e.g. `33.33,33.33,33.34`)
  and must be positive; `--exact` values follow the amount rules (positive,
  ≤ 2 decimals).
- `DESCRIPTION` is a single argument (quote multi-word descriptions).
- Empty `settle` result is `[]`; a member with no entries has `history` `[]`.
- `--currency` omitted means the base currency.
- A foreign amount that converts to 0 base cents is an error.
- Names are matched with `str.casefold`; leading/trailing whitespace is
  stripped from new names.
- JSON output uses `ensure_ascii=False` so names like "Zoë" print readably
  (default separators otherwise, so the example shapes are unchanged).
- A description starting with `-` needs the usual `--` separator.

## Left to the builder

Module internals, exact JSON storage schema, error message wording, test
structure.

  10.00 with `A=1,B=2` → A 3.34, B 6.66.
- **`--percent A=60,B=40`**: values must total exactly 100; handled as
  weights exactly like shares (portion `floor(T × p / 100)`, leftovers in
  listed order).
- **`--exact A=30,B=20`**: values are in the expense's own currency and must
  add up exactly to the expense amount (else error); then they are treated as
  weights on `T` exactly like shares.
- Only one of `--among`, `--exact`, `--shares`, `--percent` per expense.
- Every name in a split must be a current member; no name may appear twice.
- Splits are computed **once, when the expense is added**, and stored. Members
  who join later are not part of earlier "everyone" expenses.
- Shares therefore always sum to exactly `T`.

### Members
- Names are **case-insensitive**: "alice" and "Alice" are the same person.
  Adding a name that matches an existing one case-insensitively is an error.
  Every command accepts any spelling; output always uses the name as first
  added.
- Names may not contain `,` or `=`. (Builder's call: also reject empty /
  whitespace-only names.)
- Join order is preserved and matters (equal splits, output order).
- `member remove` is refused if the person appears anywhere: as payer or
  sharer of any expense, or sender/recipient of any payment. Removing someone
  with no history is fine.

### Payments
- `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT [--currency C] [--date D]`: FROM's balance goes
  up by the base amount, TO's goes down. FROM and TO the same person is an
  error. Both must be members.

### Balances
- For each member: `Σ(base amounts they paid) − Σ(their shares) +
  Σ(payments sent) − Σ(payments received)`. Positive = owed money.

### Settle (greedy, deterministic)
While anyone has a nonzero balance: the person who owes the most (most
negative) pays the person who is owed the most (most positive) the smaller of
the two absolute amounts, so at least one of them reaches zero. Ties on either
side go to the name that comes first alphabetically, ignoring case
(`str.casefold`). Payments are listed in the order they are worked out.
`settle` only suggests; it records nothing.

### Dates and categories
- `--date YYYY-MM-DD`, validated as a real date; default is today.
- `--category`, default `"other"`.

### IDs
- Expenses are numbered 1, 2, 3, … ; an ID is never reused, even after
  removal (store a `next_id` counter).

## Commands and output

Reporting commands print JSON via `json.dumps` with default separators (which
matches the examples below exactly), followed by a newline.

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `init CUR` | nothing |
| `member add NAME` / `member remove NAME` | nothing |
| `member list` | `["Alice", "Bob"]` (join order) |
| `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION [opts]` | the new ID alone, e.g. `1` |
| `expense list` | see below (ID order) |
| `expense remove ID` | nothing; unknown ID is an error |
| `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT [--currency] [--date]` | nothing |
| `rate set CUR RATE` | nothing |
| `balances` | `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}` |
| `settle` | `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]` |
| `history NAME` | `[{"date": ..., "description": ..., "change": ..., "balance": ...}]` |
| `report` | `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}` |
| `export FILE` | nothing; writes CSV |

`expense list` entry:
`{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner",
"amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category":
"food", "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}` — `amount` is in the
expense's own currency, everything else in base. `shares` keys are in split
order.

`history NAME`: every expense where the person is payer or sharer, and every
payment they sent or received, sorted by date then by the order added
(expenses and payments share one insertion sequence). `change` is their
balance change from that entry; `balance` is the running total. Expense lines
use the expense description; payments use `"Payment to Alice"` (sender's view)
or `"Payment from Bob"` (recipient's view). A payer with no share still gets a
line. The final `balance` equals that person's `balances` value.

`report`: for each category, each person's total **share** (not what they
paid) of expenses in that category. Payments are excluded.

`export FILE`: CSV with header `id,date,payer,description,amount,currency,category,base_amount`,
one row per expense in ID order, money as two-decimal strings. Overwrites
FILE if it exists.

## Errors

- Any error: message to **stderr**, exit status **1**, and `kitty.json` is
  **left unchanged** (validate fully before writing; write atomically via a
  temp file + rename).
- Includes argparse usage errors (override its default exit status 2).
- Any command other than `init` when `kitty.json` doesn't exist is an error;
  `init` when it already exists is an error.
- An unreadable or malformed `kitty.json` is an error, not a traceback.

## Storage

`kitty.json` (builder may refine the exact schema): base currency, rates
(as decimal strings), members in join order, expenses and payments each with a
shared insertion sequence number, stored rate, original amount in cents,
base amount in cents, and stored shares as an ordered list of `[name, cents]`;
plus `next_id`. Money stored as integer cents so nothing is re-rounded on
reload.

## Calls I made (user can override)

- Mutating commands other than `expense add` print nothing on success.
- `report`: categories in alphabetical order; within each, only people who
  had a share in that category, in join order. `balances` includes every
  current member, in join order.
- Category is stored as typed (so `Food` and `food` are different categories).
- Rates may have any number of decimal places.
- `--percent` values may have up to two decimals (e.g. `33.33,33.33,33.34`)
  and must be positive; `--exact` values follow the amount rules (positive,
  ≤ 2 decimals).
- `DESCRIPTION` is a single argument (quote multi-word descriptions).
- Empty `settle` result is `[]`; a member with no entries has `history` `[]`.
- `--currency` omitted means the base currency.
- A foreign amount that converts to 0 base cents is an error.
- Names are matched with `str.casefold`; leading/trailing whitespace is
  stripped from new names.
- JSON output uses `ensure_ascii=False` so names like "Zoë" print readably
  (default separators otherwise, so the example shapes are unchanged).
- A description starting with `-` needs the usual `--` separator.
